predecessors.name: Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg
predecessors.text: the Lüneburg half of the Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg: 'the Principality of Lüneburg emerged as a result of the division of Brunswick-Lüneburg in 1269'; about 11,000 km2 'including the larger part of…

successors.name: Electorate of Hanover
successors.text: the principality, 'merged into the Electorate of Brunswick-Lüneburg' on the death of Duke George William in 1705

ledger.x: 1269: the Principality of Lüneburg emerges from the division of Brunswick-Lüneburg.
1370: Charles IV gives Lüneburg to the Saxe-Wittenberg dukes.
28 May 1388: Henry wins at Winsen an der Aller.
1617: Grubenhagen returns to the Celle line.
1665: after Christian Louis's death George William cedes Grubenhagen (and Calenberg) to his brother John.
28 August 1705: the Principality of Lüneburg passes to the Electorate.

wars.name: War of the Lüneburg Succession
wars.outcome: Welf victory at Winsen an der Aller on 28 May 1388; the inheritance agreement of 1389 secured the principality for the Welfs.

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed or treaty frontier; the extent is the 1409 description (Lüneburg Heath and the Wendland, about 11,000 km2) carried through the life.
